title: [R3-7] Fence the project active-graph slot inside the activation decision
description:
FILED FROM THE THIRD HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #3 (anchored d01c3316, 2026-08-28: 'Request changes - do not merge', 12 P1 merge blockers + P2 follow-ups). Re-verified at HEAD a09b11fa by a read-only verifier; see the ruling memo in the epic channel. Reviewer's finding: R3-7 activation split-brain. Existing rows checked: task-eacea969d636420b8f5c47304039e056(DONE) closesIt=false, task-9e52f850959342faa3d464eed3c35f34(DONE) closesIt=false, task-b6cae247d19c49a180be21d011346421(DONE) closesIt=false, task-4247169c97734dfca286c1008f5f0745(DONE) closesIt=false, task-c289b8fbcb9840968a9b3994e73b79a4(BLOCKED) closesIt=false. Gap this row closes: No open or done row adds a project-scoped fenced aggregate to the activation decision. Thirteen board queries (split brain activation; project-wide active fenced; concurrent activation different goals; active slot aggregate; PROJECT_HAS_ACTIVE; graph activation race; second ACTIVE revision; R3-7; activation wedged project; project-scoped fenced aggregate incl. archived; active graph incl. archived; graph supersede incl. archived; store lock exclusive process) returned no owner, and the full 93-row listing of epic-072d85bea56c4badb07b9356ae195a98 contains no activation or split-brain row. The originating row explicitly disclaimed ownership of the fence and nothing picked it up; the broker store-lock rows are Windows launch-time exclusivity, not a store invariant. R3-7 is unowned.

REVIEWER (PR #3 review 3, anchored d01c3316, P1 merge blocker R3-7): concurrent different-goal activations can durably create project split-brain. The active-graph check is a pre-transaction scan; the source acknowledges different goals share no fenced aggregate and can both commit ACTIVE revisions (apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-revision-activation-leg.ts:123-146). The transaction has no project-wide active-slot leg (apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-activation-service.ts:199-217). Later reads fail closed, but the project is already durably wedged.

RE-MEASURED AT HEAD a09b11fa (both files clean, zero commits since d01c3316, lines identical): `projectHasActive` (leg.ts:136-147) enumerates `graph-revision:<projectId>:` through `enumerateAggregateIdsByPrefix` (packages/store/src/event-read-model.ts:66) and replays siblings at leg.ts:224-225, before any transaction; the store's only `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` is packages/store/src/decision-ledger-transaction.ts:127 inside `commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs`, reached from service.ts:217, and under the lock packages/store/src/decision-ledger-legs.ts:79-82 compares only each leg's own tail version. The legs at service.ts:199-216 are the goal (per goal), the revision (`graph-revision:<project>:<revisionId>` at expectedVersion 0, leg.ts:238) and optionally the budget genesis root, which budget-genesis-leg.ts:148-164 keys per goal. Nothing project-scoped is fenced. In-process interleaving cannot happen (synchronous `node:sqlite` DatabaseSync, no worker_threads, `runGraphEdge` at daemon-command-graph-edges.ts:147-149 reads and commits in one synchronous call); a genuine cross-process race is reachable because the store opens WAL with busy_timeout 5000 and no exclusive locking mode (sqlite-event-store.ts:149-215) and four non-test modules open stores. The existing arm graph-activation-service.test.ts:195-198 concedes the single-handle fixture cannot reach the fence. The originating row task-eacea969 recorded 'Closing it needs a project-scoped fenced aggregate this row does not own' and no row was filed. The broker store lock (task-b6cae247, task-4247169c) is Windows opcode-3 launch-time exclusivity whose DoD says ordinary launches take no lock; it is not a store invariant.

FIX SHAPE (one thing): a project-scoped active-graph SLOT aggregate whose id lives outside the `graph-revision:<projectId>:` prefix and outside `moe-internal:`. Every initial activation (service.ts extraLegs) and every replacement supersession (graph-supersede-service.ts:145-147) APPENDS one slot event naming the revision it makes ACTIVE, under `expectedVersion` = the slot version OBSERVED in the same synchronous pass as `projectHasActive`. Two writers that both passed the scan then both claim the same slot version and the store's per-leg fence (decision-ledger-legs.ts:79-82) rejects the loser with the slot as refusing aggregate, zero residue. The store already supports this: `ExpectedVersionDecisionLeg` (packages/store/src/decision-legs-contracts.ts:16-20), MAX_DECISION_LEGS 8 (approve goes to 3-4 legs, supersede 6 to 7). `projectHasActive` stays as the fast coded refusal (GRAPH_REVISION_PROJECT_HAS_ACTIVE); the read-side ACTIVE_GRAPH_SPLIT_BRAIN detector stays as defense in depth. Operator recovery of an already-wedged store is NOT this row.
definitionOfDone: Red first from a cross-handle interleaving arm on the REAL SqliteEventStore: two store handles opened on one WAL file (or a commit-seam facade on handle A whose first `commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs` runs the peer's complete `activateApprovedGraph` for a DIFFERENT goal and revision on handle B, after A's `projectHasActive` scan and before A's own commit). At HEAD the arm must red by producing two ACTIVE revisions and `readCurrentActiveGraph` answering ACTIVE_GRAPH_SPLIT_BRAIN; record that red with its count line. After the fix the loser's decision is REJECTED with the refusing aggregate equal to the slot aggregate id, the loser's goal has zero GoalExecutionEnabled events, the loser's revision aggregate is at version 0, the event horizon moved only by the winner's legs, and `readCurrentActiveGraph` returns the winner's revision. DRILL: delete the slot leg from `extraLegs` at graph-activation-service.ts:214-216 and confirm exactly this arm reds with two ACTIVE revisions.

The slot leg's expectedVersion is the OBSERVED slot version read in the same synchronous pass as `projectHasActive`, never a constant, and the slot is an APPEND leg: a second-lifetime arm (an initial activation on a project whose slot already advanced through an activation plus a supersession, i.e. slot version >= 2 after the prior ACTIVE was retired or in a fixture that seeds the slot ahead) accepts and advances the slot by exactly one. DRILL A: hard-code the slot expectedVersion to 0 and confirm the second-lifetime arm reds. DRILL B: replace the slot leg with a read-only fence (`events: []`) and confirm the cross-handle interleaving arm of clause 1 reds because the slot version never moves. Each drill is run alone, then production is restored to its recorded SHA256 with an empty diff.

graph.supersede appends to the SAME slot under the same observed-version rule (graph-supersede-service.ts:145-147; total legs 7, asserted <= MAX_DECISION_LEGS): an approve-versus-supersede cross-handle interleaving arm (handle B supersedes the current ACTIVE between handle A's scan and A's initial activation of a fresh goal) leaves exactly one ACTIVE revision and the loser rejected on the slot. DRILL: remove the slot leg from the supersede decision only, confirm this arm reds while clause 1's approve arm stays green (one degree of freedom), restore.

The slot aggregate id is asserted by test to start with neither `graph-revision:<projectId>:` nor `moe-internal:`, and a project whose only aggregate is the slot still answers `projectHasActive` null and `readCurrentActiveGraph` ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT. DRILL: rename the slot id to begin with `graph-revision:<projectId>:` and confirm the write-side scan reds with GRAPH_REVISION_SIBLING_UNREADABLE and the read-side arm reds with a replay refusal; restore.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` exit 0, run standalone and unpiped, with nonzero count lines recorded in a task comment; the pre-existing ONE-ACTIVE drill from task-eacea969 (neuter `projectHasActive`) still reds its arm, proving the pre-scan was kept beneath the fence; any decision-leg roster or evidence expectation that pinned the activation decision's leg list is updated for the extra leg with the pin's own drill, not by loosening the codec; explicit-pathspec commit with the task id in every describe title.
taskRails: Never delete or weaken `projectHasActive` or the read-side ACTIVE_GRAPH_SPLIT_BRAIN detector; the slot fence is added beneath them.

The slot aggregate id must not share the `graph-revision:<projectId>:` prefix (both leg.ts:141 and active-graph-projection.ts:131 enumerate by that prefix and would replay the slot as an unreadable sibling) and must not start with `moe-internal:` (decision-ledger-transaction.ts:73 refuses it).
The slot's expectedVersion is read in the same synchronous pass as the scan; introduce no `await` or worker thread into `runGraphEdge`, `activateApprovedGraph`, or `supersedeActiveGraph`.

The loser must surface as the store's own expected-version rejection naming the slot as refusing aggregate; if a daemon-layer code is added anyway, move the `GRAPH_REVISION_ACTIVATION_CODES` length pin at graph-activation-refusals.test.ts:83 deliberately with its drill, never by deleting the pin.
Keep total legs <= MAX_DECISION_LEGS (8) on both decisions; do not fold the slot into an existing leg or change packages/store.

Cross-handle arms must run against a real SqliteEventStore over one WAL file or a commit-seam facade on a real store; a single-handle sequential arm cannot reach the window (graph-activation-service.test.ts:195-198 already says so) and does not satisfy clause 1.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-revision-activation-leg.ts, graph-activation-service.ts, graph-supersede-service.ts, a new slot module plus tests and fixtures under apps/daemon/src/planning; the fixture must gain a second goal with its own sealed approvable run in the same project (graph-activation-test-fixtures.ts today carries one GOAL_ID).
Operator recovery of an already split-brained store is out of scope; file it separately if the QA loop demands it.
Adopt, never duplicate: re-measure the cited lines at claim time; if a sibling row landed the mechanism first, verify and close rather than re-implement.
